newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up near day's highs.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up near day's highs.

text.p: French stocks finished higher on Wednesday in line with other European markets, which were buoyed by a new record set on Wall Street and the dollar's strength.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 29.93 points, or 1.3 percent, at 2,331.62 after breaching a zone of mild resistance around 2,325 points. After backsliding for weeks on signs of volatility in the U.S. stockmarket, the index is again poised to tackle its all-time record of 2,360.98 points.
But brokers said a big move forward was unlikely before key U.S. economic indicators are issued on Thursday and Friday.
The CAC-40 January futures contract rose 32 points to 2,337.
"It was a lovely trading session today with lots of volume thanks to the recovery last night on Wall Street and most of all to the rise in the dollar," a trader said.
Trading was a heavy 6.4 billion francs.

* Shares in luxury goods group LVMH rose 3.11 percent to 1,460 francs. Dealers and portfolio managers said they expect brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu to issue a favourable report soon on the group, taking into account the acquisition of duty free chain DFS. U.S. antitrust authorities are expected to issue their decision on the deal soon, possibly next week.
A rise in shares in Italian family-controlled jeweller Bulgari fuelled rumours that LVMH may be preparing a bid, but the group denied that it was interested in Bulgari.

* Dassault Aviation finished up 7.42 percent at 1,259 francs, and Dassault Electronique rose 5.38 percent to 490 francs on the latest developments in the restructuring of the French aerospace and defence industries.

A defence ministry official said state-owned Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation would be merged in the spring, and the group would subsequently be privatised. The government asked the privatisation commission to decide on the parities.

The newspaper La Tribune said the Aerospatiale-Dassault group may team up with engineering group Alcatel Alsthom to bid for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF. Alcatel shares rose 3.06 percent to 427.50 francs.

* Shares in food group Danone rose 3.49 percent to 742 francs after brokerage UBS raised its recommendation on the stock to buy from hold. It said Danone was undervalued by 20 percent in comparison with foreign competitors, such as Unilever, and in relation to the Paris bourse.
Danone denied a market rumour that it might be interested in Italy's Parmalat Finanziaria.

* Rhone-Poulenc closed off 2.18 percent to 166.20 francs on speculation that a shareholder was preparing to place around 15 million shares, or five percent of the capital. The seller was rumoured to be CDR, the state agency grouping Credit Lyonnais assets to be sold. CDR and Rhone declined comment.

* Brokers expect investors to hug the sidelines ahead of U.S. December wholesale prices due on Thursday and unemployment figures due on Friday. "The bourse is totally tied to Wall Street," one trader said. "The U.S. influence will be even more pronounced as we're waiting for producer prices on Thursday and jobs data on Friday."
